question: Another serious incident has occurred involving arbitrary and illegal checks being carried out by ‘officials’ of the occupying regime in schools in occupied Rizokarpaso, where a small number of enclaved Greeks still live despite the adverse conditions there.

Specifically, the occupying authorities entered the Greek schools in Rizokarpaso unannounced (kindergarten, primary school and six-grade secondary school) and began inspecting books, classrooms and computers and interrogating teachers about the curriculum.

The occupying authorities have repeatedly carried out various illegal actions in schools in Rizokarpaso, obstructing education and hindering staffing and forbidding visits by inspectors from the Cypriot Ministry of Education, building repairs and other forms of support. These actions are a flagrant violation of the Third Vienna Agreement and the binding Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union.
In light of the great disappointment at the position of the European Commission, which should not show tolerance in the face of such serious matters, can it answer the following: 1.
Is it aware of these acts of interference and, more generally, the climate of intimidation and fear that schools in Rizokarpaso are being subjected to?
Given that the situation of oppression is getting worse, is it considering taking steps other than contacts and recommendations, which have proven fruitless?
Does it intend to publicly denounce the actions of the occupying regime, as a gesture of solidarity towards European pupils, parents and teachers?

Joint answer given by Ms Ferreira on behalf of the European Commission (13 June 2024) The Commission is aware of the situation of the Greek Cypriot schools in Rizokarpaso. The Commission encourages both communities in Cyprus to abide fully by the provisions of the 1975 Third Vienna Agreement (1), and will continue to monitor the situation.

The situation emphasises the urgent need to reach a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus issue. The Commission welcomes the recent appointment of the United Nations (UN) Secretary-General’s Personal Envoy on Cyprus who is seeking common ground between the two communities. The EU stands ready to play an active role in supporting all stages of the UN-facilitated process, with all appropriate means at its disposal.

The EU remains fully committed to a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus problem within the UN framework, on the basis of a bicommunal, bizonal federation with political equality, in accordance with all relevant UN Security Council resolutions and in line with the principles on which the EU is founded and the acquis.

The United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus (UNFICYP) has long-standing contacts with the Greek Cypriots and Maronites residing in the Turkish Cypriot community, regularly delivering humanitarian assistance to them. It also engages with the education authorities of the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish Cypriot local bodies to ensure the functioning of the Greek Cypriot schools in Rizokarpaso.
